<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <meta name="color-scheme" content="light">
  <meta name="theme-color" content="#fff">
  <meta name="description" content="A single black circle centered on a white page.">
  <title>Black circle</title>
  <style>
    *, *::before, *::after {
      box-sizing: border-box;
      margin: 0;
      padding: 0;
    }
    body {
      min-height: 100vh;
      min-height: 100dvh;
      display: grid;
      place-items: center;
      background: #fff;
    }
    svg {
      display: block;
      width: min(400px, 90vmin);
      height: auto;
    }
    @media (forced-colors: active) {
      circle { fill: CanvasText; }
    }
  </style>
  <link rel="icon" href="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 2 2'%3E%3Ccircle cx='1' cy='1' r='1'/%3E%3C/svg%3E">
</head>
<body>
  <main>
    <svg width="400" height="400" viewBox="0 0 400 400" role="img" aria-labelledby="circle-title">
      <title id="circle-title">Black circle</title>
      <circle cx="200" cy="200" r="200" fill="#000"/>
    </svg>
  </main>
</body>
</html>

I didn't change anything. `0.html` is already in good shape, and any edit I could make would just be churn. It already has:

- **Valid, minimal markup:** a proper doctype, `lang`, charset, viewport and description.
- **Accessibility:** the SVG has `role="img"` and a title linked with `aria-labelledby`. There's a `forced-colors` fallback so the circle stays visible in Windows High Contrast mode.
- **Responsive sizing:** `min(400px, 90vmin)` keeps the circle in view on any screen. `100dvh`, with `100vh` as a fallback, handles mobile browser toolbars.
- **Stable layout while loading:** the `width`/`height` attributes reserve space before the CSS is applied.
- **No extra requests:** the favicon is built into the page.

If you tell me what you're after, I can take it further. Some options:

1. **Dark mode:** invert the colors when the system prefers dark (right now it's locked to light).
2. **Motion or interaction:** a subtle pulse (which would respect `prefers-reduced-motion`) or a response to hover or click.
3. **A different look:** a gradient, an outline-only circle or other shapes.
4. **Sharper edges:** turn off anti-aliasing with `shape-rendering="geometricPrecision"` or `crispEdges`. It's a small visual difference.

Which direction do you want?
